body:
Stopped before claiming #1862 because its required dependencies #1860 and #1861 are unavailable on an allowed base.
Upstream main 6f8b309dcea9ea2c367ecfa53261ed140881bab3 has no crates/geometry/src/dxf reader or the requested DXF sketch-chaining implementation.
#1860 is open. Its latest comment reports uncommitted work, with no push or PR.
#1861 is open. Its latest comment reports that it stopped because #1860 is unavailable.
The open-PR search found no PR for either prerequisite to stack on.
Implementing those prerequisites here would exceed the instruction to work only #1862.
No claim, worktree, code change, pinning test, or gate run was made for #1862. The per-file overlap check was not started.
The next attempt needs both prerequisites on an allowed base, within the one-level stacking limit.

The maintainer added this to the DXF work in chat on 2026-11-15.

His words: "A DXF should be possible to "place" on a stock and used as references for cutting - not be treated like a model - thus for processes like wireedm, plasma, laser, etc etc.. we can just make a sheet, cube, cylinder. place the DXF - and select operations accordingly. The Adding DXF Profile, should thus live on "Stock page" and have a "virtual" model reference, just so the operations pages gets happy about a model being loaded.."

Change to the scope of this issue:

1. A DXF drawing is a profile that the user places on the stock of a setup. It is not a model.
2. A setup with a stock (a sheet, a block or a cylinder) and no model is a legal setup. The user makes the stock, places the DXF profile on it, and adds operations.
3. The `Sketch` entity belongs to the setup. Its `Location` is relative to the stock: the default is the top face of the stock, at the stock origin. The user can move and rotate it on that face.
4. The command adds the profile to a setup (`ImportDxf` gets the setup as an argument). Undo removes it. The MCP tool and the script verb get the same argument.
5. The setup gets a virtual model reference when it has a placed profile and no model. Each check that asks "is a model loaded" accepts that reference. The reference has no facets, thus 3D solid tools never read it as a mesh.
6. The gouge, collision and verify checks must not pass silently because the model is virtual. Each operation on a sketch states what it checks against (the stock and the sketch chains). An operation that needs a solid model refuses by name on a virtual reference.
7. Record the design of the virtual reference in `docs/decisions/`: what it is in the ECS, what the project file stores, and which checks read it.

Done means, in addition to the list in the issue body:

- A setup with only a stock and a placed DXF profile saves, loads, and accepts a 2D operation on the sketch chains.
- A 3D operation on that setup refuses with a message that names the missing solid model.
- Pins: the placement on the stock top, the move on the stock, undo and redo, and the two refusals.

The UI part of this change is on #1863.

claimed: issue-worker-max (claude-fable-5-2) · 2026-11-16T05:48Z · worktree/branch issue/1862-sketch-import-dxf (stacked on #2106) · plan: Sketch component owned by a setup, placed on the stock top; undoable ImportDxf(setup, path, units) + import_dxf MCP tool + cam.importDxf; project-file round trip; virtual model reference with named refusals; open design points listed in the PR
fix on issue/1862-sketch-import-dxf · PR #2134 · pinned by sketch_profile (7 tests), sketch_project (3 tests), mcp_dxf (2 tests), sketch_data (8 tests) · merges at the next cut

PR #2134 is a draft. It is stacked on #2106. It writes project file version 63 (PR #2077 and PR #2126 also take 63; the PR that merges second takes the next number).

What the PR does for the scope change of 2026-11-15:

- A DXF drawing is a `Sketch` entity that belongs to a setup. It is not a model and has no facets.
- Its `Location` is relative to the top face of the stock of the setup, at the stock origin. `MoveSketch` moves and turns it on that face. A moved stock carries it.
- `ImportDxf` gets the setup as an argument. The MCP tool `import_dxf` and the script verb `cam.importDxf` get the same argument.
- The virtual model reference is derived from the world: a setup has one when it has a placed profile and the document has no part. Nothing is stored for it. `docs/decisions/1862-sketch-profile.md` has the design.
- A 2D operation with a profile as its source is accepted. A kind that needs a solid model refuses a profile by name. A 3D operation in a setup with only a stock and a profile refuses and names the missing solid model.

Open design questions. The PR does the specified part and does not guess these:

1. Toolpath from the chains. The PR accepts a 2D operation on a profile at each command door. It does not generate a toolpath from the chains; issue 1864 has that work. Until then, generation refuses by name and says what the operation is checked against (the stock and the chains). Is this the correct split between #1862 and #1864?
2. Top of Model and Bottom of Model on a virtual reference. The PR refuses these heights by name, because a reference with no solid has no top and no bottom. The alternative is a value (for example the stock top and the stock bottom). That changes cut depths.
3. "The stock origin". The PR reads it as the origin of the stock entity: the centre in XY for a box and a cylinder. The alternative is a stock corner or the WCS origin.
4. The kinds that take a profile. The PR admits the 2D milling, plasma and wire EDM sections. Drilling from DXF circles, turning and sinker EDM refuse a profile by name.
5. `MoveSketch` in place of `MoveModel`. The issue body said `MoveModel`. A profile has a face placement (X, Y, angle), so the PR adds `MoveSketch`, and `MoveModel` refuses a profile by name.
6. A profile that is larger than the stock or off its edge is not refused at placement. Issue 1864 has the check of the chains against the stock.

A note for issue 1863: the operation page lists models only as sources. An operation on a profile shows the stock as its source in that page until issue 1863 adds the profiles to the list. `sketch_model::model_loaded` and `sketch_model::of` are the functions for the pages. The typed error for the units prompt is `CommandError::DxfUnitsMissing { width, height }`.
